questions.q: Your app imports createRouter from @zudojs/http. You want to know exactly how it matches routes in the version you run. Where do you read?
questions.explain: The published package has no src folder, and main on GitHub may be ahead of the version you installed. The code that runs is the compiled dist JavaScript, reached through the exports map.
options: The src folder of the main branch on GitHub
The JavaScript in node_modules/@zudojs/http/dist, starting from the entry point listed in its package.json
The package's README, because it is generated from the code

questions.q: In your editor, "Go to definition" on matchesEventType opens eventType.type.d.ts. It shows only a signature. Where is the behaviour?
questions.explain: tsc writes one .js and one .d.ts for every source file, side by side. The .d.ts is the contract, the .js is what runs. The @zudojs packages ship their own types, so there is no @types package.
options: Nowhere: declaration files are compiled away
In eventType.type.js, the file with the same name next to it in dist

questions.q: Every dist file of a @zudojs package ends with //# sourceMappingURL=….js.map, yet your debugger steps through the compiled JavaScript instead of TypeScript. Why?
questions.explain: The comment points at a file that is not in the tarball. The published files list contains !dist/**/*.map. Since dist is unminified tsc output with comments, stepping through it is still comfortable.
options: Source maps only work in browsers
The files field excludes dist/**/*.map, so the maps were never published
Node.js ignores source maps for ES modules

questions.q: You try import { withRetry } from "@zudojs/adapters/dist/adapter/adapter.retry.js" and get ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED. What does it mean?
questions.explain: An exports map is an allow-list of importable paths. Anything not in it is private to the package, and Node enforces that. The file is there, and it does export withRetry; it is simply not part of the public API.
options: The file does not exist on disk
The package's exports map does not list that path, so Node refuses to load it even though the file exists
The function is not exported from its file
You need to add "type": "module" to your package.json

questions.q: @zudojs/adapters exports about 20 names and @zudojs/http well over a thousand. What difference in their dist/index.js explains most of the gap?
questions.explain: export * forwards every export of a file, including helpers nobody meant to publish. A named re-export publishes exactly the listed names. The first makes internals reachable; it does not make them public.
options: http's barrel uses many export * from lines, which re-export everything in those files, while adapters lists each public name with export { … } from

questions.q: Which names can your application safely depend on across minor and patch releases?
questions.explain: Reachable is not the same as promised. Semantic versioning covers the documented API. Exported internals, @internal members and "internal" folders can change in any release.
options: Every name that has a .d.ts declaration
Names that are exported through the exports map and documented as part of the package's API

questions.q: The container's declarations show a resolveInScope method marked @internal. TypeScript lets you call it, and it would save you some code. What should you do?
questions.explain: @internal is the author telling you the member can change without notice. Read it freely to understand behaviour, but build on the documented methods.
options: Call it: if TypeScript allows it, it is public
Call it through a relative path into node_modules
Use the public API (createScope() and resolve) and read resolveInScope only to understand how scopes work
Copy the whole container into your project

questions.q: A package depends on one package at level 0 and one at level 2. With the lesson's definition, what is its level?
questions.explain: Level is 1 plus the highest level of any dependency: 1 + max(0, 2) = 3. That guarantees every dependency is on a lower level.

questions.q: Every published @zudojs package pins its internal dependencies exactly, for example "@zudojs/errors": "1.3.2". Your own package.json asks for a newer @zudojs/errors. What does npm do?
questions.explain: An exact pin cannot be satisfied by any other version, so npm nests a second copy. Two copies means two BaseError classes and two sets of module-level state. Keep all @zudojs packages from one release and check with npm ls @zudojs/errors.
options: Installs only your version and ignores the pin
Installs both versions: yours at the top, the pinned one nested under the packages that need it
Installs only the pinned version and warns

questions.q: A diagram in the repository shows @zudojs/core depending on almost every other package. The published package.json of core lists only errors and constants. You are tracing what core can call. Which do you trust?
questions.explain: A package can only import what is installed for it, and the manifest decides that. Diagrams and conventions files describe intentions; when they disagree with the manifest, the manifest is what runs.
options: The diagram, because it describes the design
The published manifest, because it decides what is installed and importable

questions.q: Two copies of @zudojs/errors are installed. A NotFoundError created by copy B is checked against copy A with error instanceof NotFoundError. Why is the result false?
questions.explain: Loading a module twice from two paths evaluates it twice, so there are two unrelated NotFoundError classes with identical code. instanceof compares identity, not shape.
options: Because each copy defines its own class objects, and instanceof checks the prototype chain against one specific class object
Because errors lose their prototype when thrown

questions.q: Why does @zudojs/errors brand its errors with Symbol.for("@zudojs/errors.BaseError") instead of Symbol("…")?
questions.explain: Each Symbol() call makes a new, unique symbol, so two copies would have two different brands. Symbol.for(key) is shared across the whole program, which is exactly what a cross-copy check needs.
options: Symbol() cannot be used as a property key
Symbol.for returns the same symbol from the global registry for the same key, so every copy of the package creates and checks the same brand
Symbol.for symbols are enumerable, so they appear in JSON

questions.q: Your HTTP error handler must recognise any ZudoJS error, even one thrown by a package that brought its own copy of @zudojs/errors. What should it test?
questions.explain: isBaseError uses instanceof first and falls back to the shared brand plus a shape check. Codes are strings, so comparing them works across copies too.

questions.q: Resolving a scoped token from the root container throws ScopedResolutionError. Following the barrels shows it is defined in @zudojs/container/dist/containerResolution/containerResolution.error.js. Where do you import it from for an instanceof check?
questions.explain: Most container errors are re-exported from @zudojs/errors, but these resolution errors are defined locally, on top of the shared ContainerError base. @zudojs/errors does not export them, and the deep path is blocked by the exports map.
options: @zudojs/container, because it is a local class of that package (extending ContainerError from @zudojs/errors)

questions.q: Inside a request you run code with requests.runWithoutContext(fn) from @zudojs/core. The request was also running inside a tenant context from @zudojs/tenancy. What does fn see?
questions.explain: Each package owns its own AsyncLocalStorage. Leaving core's store does nothing to tenancy's. Work that must not belong to the tenant has to leave that store too.
options: No request context and no tenant
No request context, but still the tenant
The request context and the tenant, because runWithoutContext only affects timers
An error, because the two stores conflict

questions.q: getDefaultStorage() in @zudojs/tenancy keeps its storage in a module-level variable. Your middleware and your repository end up importing two different copies of the package. What happens?
questions.explain: A module-level variable exists once per loaded copy of the module. Two copies, two AsyncLocalStorage instances: get() on one never returns what run() on the other stored. It is the same duplicate-package problem as with errors.
options: They share one storage, because AsyncLocalStorage is global
They get two different storages, so the repository never sees the tenant the middleware set
Node refuses to load the second copy
The second copy throws on import

questions.q: You find createRouteTree in the exports of @zudojs/http and want to know whether createRouter uses it. What settles the question?
questions.explain: Search from the entry point you use, following real calls and imports. An exported, promising name proves nothing: here it is unused by the router and gives different answers.
options: Its name: "route tree" must be what the router uses
Tracing from createRouter: its match method calls sortedRoutes() and matchCompiledRoute, and no file outside the tree's folder imports the tree
Counting how many times the word "tree" appears in dist

questions.q: HttpRouter.match starts with const candidates = this.sortedRoutes();, and sortedRoutes returns [...this.routes].sort(…). What does that tell you?
questions.explain: The spread and sort run inside match. For a few hundred routes that is still fast, but it is worth knowing before you generate thousands of routes.
options: Routes are sorted once, when they are registered
The route table is copied and sorted on every match, so the cost of matching grows with the number of routes
The router uses a tree, so matching cost is constant
The sort only happens for OPTIONS requests

questions.q: Three instances of your API run behind a load balancer, each with an in-memory CacheService. The rate entry expires and 300 requests arrive, 100 per instance. How many loads run?
questions.explain: inFlight is a Map field of one CacheService object, so it deduplicates within one process: one load per instance. Exactly-once across servers needs a shared lock.

questions.q: AdapterRegistry.startAll() throws an AggregateError because the second of three adapters failed. What is the state of the other two?
questions.explain: The registry's loop catches each failure, continues with the next adapter and throws all failures at the end. It does not roll back. PluginManager and the lifecycle manager do; you must know which one you are calling.
options: Both were started and then stopped automatically
Both were started and are still running, until you call stopAll()

questions.q: What does a characterization test of getOrSet in your project claim?
questions.explain: A characterization test records existing behaviour, right or wrong. Its value is the alarm it raises when a new version behaves differently.
options: That getOrSet still behaves the way your code relies on, so an upgrade that changes it fails your build
That the package's own tests pass

questions.q: You found that createRouteTree matches differently from createRouter. Which report helps the maintainers most?
questions.explain: A minimal reproduction with actual and expected output leaves nothing to interpret. Editing files in node_modules is lost on the next install and helps nobody else.
options: "The route tree is broken, please fix."
The installed versions, a runnable script of about ten lines, its actual output, the expected output, and why it matters
A screenshot of your application's error page

questions.q: Both @zudojs/transactions and @zudojs/database export createTransactionContext. What is the risk?
questions.explain: Same name, different meaning. Always check the import line when an editor adds it for you, and read the .d.ts of the one you picked.
options: None: they are the same function re-exported
They do different things (an AsyncLocalStorage-backed store versus a plain record with an id and start time), so an editor auto-import can pick the wrong one
TypeScript merges them into one overloaded function

questions.q: This is the matching logic from @zudojs/events, copied. What does it print?
questions.explain: The bare namespace matches through type === namespace. orders.paid fails because the prefix includes the dot. A wildcard covers every depth, because the test is startsWith.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Normalization trims, lower-cases, turns /, \ and : into dots, collapses repeated separators and removes them at both ends.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Order:Paid is normalized to order.paid before matching, so the exact handler and the namespace wildcard both run, in registration order since their priorities are equal. invoice.* does not match.

questions.q: This copies the router's ranking rule: compare segments from the left, literal 3, parameter 2, wildcard 1. In which order are the patterns sorted?
questions.explain: The first segment decides first: the two /admin routes (literal) come before the two parameter routes. Between them, users (literal) beats *rest. Between the parameter routes, orders (literal) beats :b. Length only matters when the shorter pattern has run out of segments.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A regex constraint does not change the score: both parameter routes tie and the first registered wins, so the :id route can never run. The literal latest beats both. Matching is case-insensitive by default.

questions.q: This is the container's scope cache, copied. What does it print?
questions.explain: Reads fall back to the parent, so the child sees the request's cart. Writes stay local, so the parent never sees the child's basket.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: The child resolves first and builds cart 1 into its own cache. The parent cannot see the child's cache, so it builds cart 2. The child then finds cart 1 in its own cache.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A scoped token on the root container has no scope cache: ScopedResolutionError. A singleton that needs a scoped dependency would keep one request's cart forever, so the resolver refuses it with CaptiveDependencyError, even inside a scope.

questions.q: This is the in-flight idea behind getOrSet, reduced to a few lines. What does it print?
questions.explain: The two concurrent usd calls share one load and eur has its own: 2. After they finish, the entry is deleted and this sketch stores no result, so the last usd call loads again: 3. The real getOrSet would have found the value in the cache by then.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: All three callers await the same promise, so one call fails for all of them. The failure is not stored and the in-flight entry is removed, so the next call loads again and succeeds; it was not served from the cache.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Symbol.for looks the key up in one global registry, so it returns the same symbol every time. Symbol() always makes a new, unique one. That is why the brand survives duplicate package copies.

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: A stopped component can only be disposed, never restarted. A failed one goes through stopping, which is where rollback happens. A ready one can stop.

questions.q: This is the adapter registry's loop, simplified. What does it print?
questions.explain: The loop records the failure and keeps going, so queue still starts. Only at the end does it throw, and nothing stops db or queue.
options:
started db
started http
started queue

questions.q: What does this print?
questions.explain: Math.max(-1, …) + 1 gives 0 for no dependencies. events is one above its highest dependency (level 1), and cqrs one above events.

questions.q: Write dependents(graph, target): every package that depends on target directly or through other packages, sorted. The program should print cqrs,events,http,testing.
questions.explain: Keep adding packages that depend on the target or on anything already found, until a full pass adds nothing. cache only depends on errors, so it is not affected. A reverse-edge breadth-first search works too.

questions.q: Write level(name): 0 for a package with no dependencies, otherwise one more than the highest level among its dependencies. The program should print app=3 http=2 logger=1 errors=0.
questions.explain: The recursion follows each dependency down to the leaves. With many packages, memoize the results in a Map so each level is computed once, as the lesson's tool does.

questions.q: Implement matches(type, pattern) with the rules of @zudojs/events: "*" matches everything, an exact pattern matches itself, and "ns.*" matches ns and every type under ns. at any depth. The program should print true true true false false.
questions.explain: The dot in namespace + "." is what stops invoices.sent from matching, and the separate type === namespace test lets the bare namespace match. A pattern without .* only matches exactly.

questions.q: Two classes simulate two copies of an error package. Write isOurError(value) so that errors from both copies are recognised, using a brand from the global symbol registry, and plain Errors are not. The program should print true true false.
questions.explain: CopyA and CopyB are different classes, so instanceof CopyA fails for CopyB errors. Symbol.for returns the same symbol everywhere, so a brand set by either copy is found by the check. This is how isBaseError works.

questions.q: Write once(key, load) so that concurrent calls with the same key share one load(), and a finished (or failed) load is forgotten so the next call loads again. The program should print shared: 2 loads and then after: 3 loads.
questions.explain: Store the promise, not the value, and store it before anything awaits, so the second caller finds it. finally removes it whether the load succeeded or failed, so a failure is never served again.

questions.q: AdapterRegistry.startAll() does not roll back. Write startOrRollback(adapters): start each adapter in order; if one throws, stop the ones already started in reverse order and rethrow. The program should print start db, start cache, stop cache, stop db, failed: port in use, one per line.
questions.explain: Remember only what really started, stop it in reverse order (the last one started may depend on the earlier ones) and rethrow so the caller still sees the failure. metrics is never started.
questions.expected:
start db
start cache
stop cache
stop db
failed: port in use

questions.q: A wildcard can only be at the end, so payment.*.failed is not a valid pattern. Subscribe to payment.* and log only events whose last segment is failed. The program should print alert payment.refund.failed and alert payment.capture.failed.
questions.explain: The handler receives the normalized type, so splitting on dots gives its segments. Checking only the last one excludes payment.failed.retry, which a simple includes("failed") would wrongly accept.

questions.q: Write a characterization check for the container: create a scope and a child scope, resolve the scoped CART in the parent first, and print PASS child sees parent cart if the child gets the same object, otherwise FAIL.
questions.explain: The order matters: the parent must resolve first, because a child that resolves first keeps its own cart. The test pins the behaviour your code relies on; if a new version changes it, this line turns into FAIL.
